entries.title: Anthropic Economic Index: New building blocks for understanding AI use
entries.summary: Adds observed AI-usage evidence to the exposure stack and motivates the repo's task-primitives sidecar.
entries.limitations: Observed Claude usage is not a full labour-market census and is still a platform-specific measure.
entries.repo_notes: Active live source in the audited exposure ensemble and a major input to the future task-native direction.

entries.title: How (un)Stable Are LLM Occupational Exposure Scores? Evidence from Multi-Model Replication
entries.summary: Replicating the Eloundou-style exposure rubric with three frontier LLMs yields a 3.6-fold divergence in mean exposure and inter-model agreement as low as 57%; downstream employment estimates vary 2.4x and can flip sign by annotating model.
entries.limitations: Measures annotator instability, not which annotation is correct; ensemble averaging across independent measures dilutes but does not remove the error.
entries.repo_notes: Disclosed in Known Limitations: affects the Eloundou and ILO components of the exposure ensemble.

entries.title: How Will AI-Driven Automation Actually Affect Jobs?
entries.summary: Argues exposure alone cannot predict displacement: output-demand price elasticity (elastic demand can expand hiring as AI cuts costs) and job dimensionality (low-task jobs are easier to automate fully) are the missing variables.
entries.limitations: Commentary rather than peer-reviewed estimation; proposes collecting new price/quantity data rather than a ready-made occupation-level measure.
entries.repo_notes: Motivates the V7 demand-persistence proxy. The proxy measures recent labour-demand persistence (momentum, vacancies, scarcity), not output-price elasticity, and does not capture dimensionality — it is a partial response to this critique, not a resolution.

entries.title: Labor market impacts of AI: A new measure and early evidence
entries.summary: Separates theoretical capability from observed exposure and emphasizes that early labour effects remain limited.
entries.limitations: Uses US outcome data and a platform-linked usage measure, so it still needs Singapore-specific interpretation.
entries.repo_notes: Primary candidate reference for promoting the shadow model beyond readiness-only governance.

entries.title: O*NET Database 30.2
entries.summary: Provides the task statements, technology skills, and job-zone context used for explanation and task matching.
entries.limitations: O*NET is US-based and enters the Singapore product mainly as explanatory or crosswalk context.
entries.repo_notes: Not a direct structural-score input, but essential for the supporting task layer and future task-native scoring.

entries.title: Task-Completion Time Horizons of Frontier AI Models
entries.summary: Tracks the current task-duration horizons of frontier models and offers a capability input for scenario calibration.
entries.limitations: The benchmark is model-centric and software-task heavy, so it is not a direct occupation impact measure.
entries.repo_notes: Useful for the forecast layer, not for the core structural score.

entries.title: Who Uses AI? Platform Selection and the Measurement of Occupational AI Exposure
entries.summary: Platform-log exposure measures conflate task-level AI applicability with the occupational composition of platform users; reweighting to BLS employment shares attenuates post-ChatGPT employment estimates by 42-93%, and swapping platforms changes coefficients 1.9x.
entries.limitations: US workforce reweighting; the direction of bias for Singapore depends on local adoption composition, which is not measured at occupation level.
entries.repo_notes: Disclosed in Known Limitations: affects the Anthropic observed-usage component of the exposure ensemble.

entries.title: AI, Productivity, and Work Quality
entries.summary: Adds evidence that AI can change both output quantity and work quality, reinforcing the need for occupation-specific augmentation priors.
entries.limitations: Experimental and workflow-specific evidence still needs careful translation into occupation-level scoring.
entries.repo_notes: Useful as a V5.1 calibration reference rather than as a direct V4.x score ingredient.

entries.title: Artificial Intelligence and the Labor Market
entries.summary: Shows that mean exposure and concentration of exposure in a few tasks can have different labour-demand implications.
entries.limitations: The repo uses a simplified concentration buffer rather than the paper's full firm-task empirical setting; the buffer magnitude (lambda = 0.20) is heuristic, not estimated from the paper's coefficients.
entries.repo_notes: Primary scientific justification for the live V7 task-concentration exposure buffer (concentration offsets labour-demand losses via within-job task reallocation).

entries.title: BLS Skills Data
entries.summary: Official 17-skill summary for occupations, built on O*NET inputs and BLS projections occupations.
entries.limitations: It is a summarized skills view, not a direct task-by-task automation score.
entries.repo_notes: Best public structured skill overlay for the US country layer.

entries.title: Canaries in the Coal Mine? Six Facts about the Recent Employment Effects of Artificial Intelligence
entries.summary: ADP payroll microdata: 13% (revised ~16% by Oct 2025) relative employment decline for ages 22-25 in the most AI-exposed occupations, concentrated where usage is automative; adjustment runs through reduced hiring of entrants, not layoffs of incumbents.
entries.limitations: US payroll data; the Feb 2026 update concedes effects are significant only from 2024 under the broadest macro controls. Entry-margin evidence, not occupation-level displacement totals.
entries.repo_notes: Primary citation for the seniority modifiers and for the hiring-margin limitation: entrant-facing and incumbent-facing risk are different objects.

entries.title: CPS Demographics by Occupation
entries.summary: Occupation-linked demographic and labor-force context drawn from the Current Population Survey.
entries.limitations: Occupation/industry classification changes reduce perfect longitudinal comparability.
entries.repo_notes: Useful for showing who is exposed and for planning transition context, not for changing the structural pressure score.

entries.title: Generative AI and Jobs: A Refined Global Index of Occupational Exposure
entries.summary: Adds a recent global occupational exposure measure aligned to international occupation codes.
entries.limitations: Still a global exposure measure rather than a Singapore outcome model.
entries.repo_notes: Included because its ISCO alignment improves crosswalk robustness for the ensemble.

entries.title: How AI is transforming work at Anthropic
entries.summary: Shows how AI changes engineering and research workflows inside Anthropic, adding a concrete adoption case study.
entries.limitations: Internal workplace evidence is highly specific to Anthropic and should not be generalized into a country labour market without adjustment.
entries.repo_notes: Useful as a contextual adoption case study and a reminder that augmentation can change task mix, learning speed, and workflow design.

entries.title: Large Language Models, Small Labor Market Effects
entries.summary: Finds small early labour-market effects from chatbot adoption despite meaningful task restructuring, supporting conservative near-term risk shrinkage.
entries.limitations: The study is Denmark-specific and examines early effects; longer-run displacement remains unresolved.
entries.repo_notes: Supports the repo's choice to keep structural risk separate from near-term or realised-risk interpretations.

entries.title: Making AI Count: The Next Measurement Frontier
entries.summary: Argues that AI measurement should become more granular, task-based, and outcome-focused than current official statistics.
entries.limitations: This is a measurement agenda rather than an occupation-scoring formula.
entries.repo_notes: Best reference for the repo's longer-run shift from heuristic confidence toward richer uncertainty and task-native measurement.

entries.title: Navigating the Jagged Technological Frontier
entries.summary: Highlights that AI gains are jagged across tasks and expertise levels rather than smooth across a whole occupation.
entries.limitations: Provides strong augmentation evidence but still within constrained experimental settings.
entries.repo_notes: Supports the repo direction of modelling augmentation as its own construct rather than as a mirror image of automation.

entries.title: Occupational Employment and Wage Statistics (OEWS)
entries.summary: Official occupation-level wage and employment statistics for the United States.
entries.limitations: OEWS is US-specific and must not be interpreted as a global wage distribution.
entries.repo_notes: Best public source for the US wage layer and the richest local wage context currently available.

entries.title: Occupational Outlook Handbook / Occupation Finder
entries.summary: Official occupation profiles used for narrative, education, and work-environment context.
entries.limitations: Designed for career guidance rather than AI-risk scoring.
entries.repo_notes: Adds the human-readable occupation narrative layer for the US market.

entries.title: Occupational Requirements Survey (ORS)
entries.summary: Official occupation requirements survey covering the physical, cognitive, and preparation demands of work.
entries.limitations: ORS is not a labour-market outcome series; it is a requirements survey used for bottleneck and friction context.
entries.repo_notes: The best current official analogue for transition friction and human-bottleneck validation in the US layer.

entries.title: The Rapid Adoption of Generative AI
entries.summary: Documents that workplace generative-AI adoption is fast, supporting a separate adoption layer in forecast models.
entries.limitations: Adoption speed alone does not identify realised labour displacement or productivity effects.
entries.repo_notes: Used to justify separating structural pressure from near-term realised-risk proxies.

entries.title: Exposure to Artificial Intelligence and Occupational Mobility: A Cross-country Analysis
entries.summary: Suggests that mobility responses to AI pressure follow structured pathways rather than generic occupational distance rules.
entries.limitations: Cross-country evidence informs the transition design, but the repo still needs a Singapore-specific mobility dataset.
entries.repo_notes: Guides the schema for observed transition priors and future ranking logic in the transition layer.

entries.title: Impact of AI on Singapore’s Labor Market
entries.summary: IMF Singapore-specific estimates: ~77% of Singapore workers are highly exposed to AI (vs ~60% advanced-economy / ~40% emerging-market averages), split roughly evenly between high- and low-complementarity exposure.
entries.limitations: Aggregate exposure/complementarity shares at the economy level, not occupation-by-occupation scores; uses the IMF exposure framework rather than this repo’s 4-source ensemble.
entries.repo_notes: The most directly relevant external benchmark for a Singapore AI-exposure product. Not yet used for formal calibration; flagged as a convergent-validity target more relevant than US BLS.

entries.title: New Frontiers: The Origins and Content of New Work, 1940-2018
entries.summary: 60% of 2018 US employment is in job titles that did not exist in 1940; new work emerges disproportionately in occupations exposed to augmenting rather than automating innovations.
entries.limitations: Historical US evidence; no AI-era occupation-level reinstatement rate yet exists that could serve as a score input.
entries.repo_notes: The canonical quantified evidence for why displacement-only scores overstate long-run risk; cited in the central limitation.

entries.title: US BLS Employment Projections 2024-2034
entries.summary: Provides the external benchmark used for convergent validation and for the BLS-weighted proxy employment field.
entries.limitations: This is US evidence and should not be interpreted as Singapore occupation outcome truth.
entries.repo_notes: Lives in the repo as both a validation benchmark and a clearly labeled external proxy.

entries.title: Generative AI at Work
entries.summary: Shows large heterogeneous productivity effects from AI assistance in a specific workflow, supporting separate augmentation modelling.
entries.limitations: The effect size is workflow-specific and should not be generalized into a universal augmentation constant.
entries.repo_notes: Candidate reference for replacing a single structural augmentation heuristic with workflow-aware priors.

entries.title: GPTs are GPTs: An Early Look at the Labor Market Impact Potential of Large Language Models
entries.summary: Frames LLM exposure around task feasibility and time-saving potential rather than broad automation narratives.
entries.limitations: The paper is early and US-oriented, and it does not by itself provide Singapore labour-market calibration.
entries.repo_notes: Used as a reference for the repo's future task-native model direction, not as a direct live source key.

entries.title: GPTs are GPTs: An Early Look at the Labor Market Impact Potential of Large Language Models
entries.summary: Provides the GPT-oriented exposure source used as one leg of the live exposure ensemble.
entries.limitations: Like other exposure indices, it measures capability overlap rather than realised displacement.
entries.repo_notes: Kept in the live ensemble because it adds an LLM-specific construct not covered by AIOE alone.

entries.title: Labor Market Exposure to AI: Cross-country Differences and Distributional Implications
entries.summary: Provides the complementarity framework that the repo operationalises as the human bottleneck layer.
entries.limitations: Designed as a broad labour-exposure framing rather than a Singapore occupation-level calibrated outcome model.
entries.repo_notes: Directly tied to the theta-based bottleneck implementation in the current scorer.

entries.title: Technology, Skills, and Globalization: Explaining International Differences in Routine and Nonroutine Work Using Survey Data
entries.summary: Worker-survey evidence across 46 countries: task content differs substantially across countries within the same occupation, so US O*NET-based task measures misstate task content abroad.
entries.limitations: Singapore is not in the PIAAC/STEP samples, so the bias cannot be directly corrected; high-income economies show smaller divergence from US task content.
entries.repo_notes: The canonical citation for the SSOC-ISCO-SOC-O*NET crosswalk caveat; motivates benchmarking against Singapore-native task data (SkillsFuture Skills Framework).

entries.title: Occupational mobility and automation: a data-driven network model
entries.publisher: Journal of the Royal Society Interface 18(174)
entries.summary: Network model on empirical occupational transitions: whether an automation shock produces unemployment or smooth reallocation depends on the topology of the transition network around an occupation, not its exposure alone.
entries.limitations: US transition-network data; Singapore-specific mobility networks are not yet measured, so the repo applies the insight via its structural transition-capacity scores.
entries.repo_notes: Grounds the high-risk x few-exits quadrant surfacing (rankings and occupation pages): escape-route quality, not pressure alone, shapes outcomes.

entries.title: Occupational, industry, and geographic exposure to artificial intelligence: A novel dataset and its potential uses
entries.summary: Provides the published AIOE occupation exposure dataset used as a baseline source in the ensemble.
entries.limitations: Measures theoretical exposure rather than realised AI use or job outcomes.
entries.repo_notes: Tied directly to the live AIOE source key and still used in the canonical exposure ensemble.

entries.title: A Method to Link Advances in Artificial Intelligence to Occupational Abilities
entries.summary: Introduces the task-ability linkage approach that underpins modern AI-exposure measurement.
entries.limitations: Provides the conceptual bridge from AI capabilities to work content, but not current observed usage or Singapore-specific outcomes.
entries.repo_notes: Referenced as the foundational exposure framework behind later AIOE-style occupation measures.

entries.title: What Works? A Meta-Analysis of Recent Active Labor Market Program Evaluations
entries.publisher: Journal of the European Economic Association 16(3)
entries.summary: Meta-analysis of 200+ active labour market programme evaluations: average training impacts are close to zero in the short run and only modestly positive 2-3 years post-programme.
entries.limitations: Pre-AI-era programmes, mostly Europe/US; Singapore schemes (SkillsFuture, SCTP, CCP) have published only selection-biased administrative outcomes, no causal evaluation.
entries.repo_notes: Grounds the caveat that transition-capacity scores measure structural skill adjacency, not evidence that retraining works.
